correctness.rationale: Direct multiplication gives ad=df=ae+bf=AD=DF=AE+BF=0 and the three stated commutator coordinates. Outside d=D=0, one nonzero middle entry forces both pairs of outer entries to vanish by the square and commutator equations, giving the affine piece E. On the slice each of M,N has rank ≤1. Substituting M=pℓᵀ,N=qmᵀ into the remaining commutator gives (p1 q2+p2 q1)(ℓ1 m2−ℓ2 m1); the factors are exactly the dependence tests for (p,Sq) and (ℓ,m). Zero matrices satisfy both rank tests. The independent witnesses d≠0, (E12,E34), and (E12,E13) distinguish the three pieces in all characteristics. The two determinantal cones have dimension 5 before the two free coordinates and are geometrically integral by outer-product parametrization (or the pivot charts); the equality of reduced closed loci follows from the exhaustion over geometric points. E∩R has six free coordinates, and E∩T adds bE+eB=0, giving dimension five and the triple intersection. Independently, in R∩T the two matrices M and SN together are (t pℓᵀ,u pℓᵀ); excluding the zero pair gives a cone over the product of three projective lines, of dimension 4 before c,C, hence dimension 6. This works with a zero block and in characteristic two. Its finite-field size before c,C is 1+(q−1)(q+1)^3. Each determinantal cone has 1+(q⁴−1)(q²−1)/(q−1)=q⁵+q⁴−q points, and E overlaps their union in E∩R. Inclusion–exclusion with these independent counts yields q⁸+2q⁷−2q⁵.

evidence: The product-fiber record already identifies the affine outside-slice stratum. On the nonzero-product slice PQ=tJ where J swaps the coordinates, it gives Q=tP^(-1)J. Since the 2×2 adjugate is linear, this makes Q proportional to adj(P)J and yields the horizontal rank-one cone T on closing. claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The affine piece and T closure can be recovered from that coordinate description. The nontrivial remainder is determining which parts of the zero-product locus form a new component rather than subsets of T, and the reduced geometry of the resulting intersections, uniformly in characteristic. The two possible rank factorizations in the frozen proof establish this, and no inspected exact classification implies it as a stated special case.

originality.rationale: Pass is for the complete reduced component and incidence description of the fixed triangular slice, not the already covered point total, coordinate reduction to the middle-zero slice, or the nonzero-product geometry in isolation. A distinct exact product-fiber record gives the same point total and the dense nonzero-product stratum of T; its parametrization also yields the determinantal model of the closure of that stratum. It does not furnish the entire zero-product geometry, the separation of the other components from that closure, or the intersection classification. The nearby classifications in unrestricted triangular and full square-zero ambient spaces likewise do not give the slice decomposition.
residual_risks: The same-day product-fiber result has real scientific overlap; neither date in a path establishes publication priority. The frozen reference list does not resolve its vague attribution of earlier prescribed-product counts. Those counts are not credited as original here.
The inspection is bounded and cannot rule out an unindexed classification of the fixed-flag restriction.

value.rationale: This is a natural fixed-flag slice of a standard square-zero commuting variety. Its classification distinguishes a larger affine component and two lower-dimensional determinantal pieces with different embeddings. The unequal pairwise incidence dimensions show concretely why counting or studying the nonzero-product stratum misses the geometry. It is useful as a complete small-rank example in all characteristics, not as a recomputation of an arithmetic invariant.
residual_risks: No downstream result at higher rank or classification of nonreduced schemes is inferred.
